node.title: Re: Perl to C problem
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
$test = " "; The code prints a string of 10s, indicating that the 13/10 combination in Windows has been translated to a bare 10.

That's because, even in Windows, only represents LF, not CRLF (that'd be )*. You can verify this using Dump from [doc://Devel::Peek], it'll show you exactly what Perl is storing internally. The only place where Perl on Windows does automatic translation between CRLF/LF is on I/O from/to a file, because there, the [doc://PerlIO|:crlf layer] is enabled by default (unless you specify the :raw layer or use [doc://binmode]). So perhaps if you're reading from a file that has CRLF endings, you might want to turn off that layer.

By the way, you might want to have a look at [http://rperl.org/|RPerl], it can take a subset of Perl and compile it.

* Update: As [Athanasius] [id://1229988|points out], see [doc://perlport#Newlines|Newlines in perlport] for even more details.
